{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are a CVE applicability analyst. You will receive JSON input with two parts: (1) system_profile, describing the installed system including OS, hardware, and a list of installed software packages with names and versions, and (2) advisories, a supplied list of CVE entries, each with an ID, a description, and affected-product information (product names, version ranges, or conditions).

Your task: identify which of the SUPPLIED advisories actually apply to the installed system. An advisory is applicable only if ALL of the following hold:
1. The affected product named in the advisory matches a product actually installed in the system inventory. Beware of similar-but-different product names (e.g., different distributions, forks, or unrelated products sharing a name fragment); do not match unrelated products.
2. The installed version of that product falls WITHIN the affected version range stated in the advisory. Pay careful attention to version boundaries: whether endpoints are included or excluded, version ordering (e.g., 1.10 vs 1.9), suffixes/pre-release tags (e.g., rc, beta, -1.el7), and whether fixes are 'before X', 'up to and including X', or 'from A through B'. If the installed version is outside the stated range (too old, too new, or an explicitly fixed/patched version), the advisory is NOT applicable.
3. Any additional conditions in the advisory (affected architecture, OS, configuration, feature, or module) are satisfied by the system profile. If a condition is not confirmable from the inventory, only include the CVE if the product and version clearly match.

Use the advisory's description and affected fields as the primary evidence; do not rely on external knowledge of CVEs. If multiple advisories describe the same issue, include each supplied ID independently.

Answer format: return ONLY a JSON object of the form {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]}. The array must contain unique identifiers taken verbatim from the supplied advisories list, with no duplicates and no IDs that were not supplied. If no advisories apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Do not include explanations, markdown, or any text outside the JSON object.

Be rigorous on both sides: do not omit CVEs that genuinely match (recall matters), and do not include CVEs whose affected versions exclude the installed version or whose affected product is not actually installed (precision matters). Input is JSON containing system_profile and advisories. Each advisory supplies its ID, description, and affected information. The answer must be a JSON object whose applicable_cves array contains unique IDs from that supplied list. Return your instruction as a JSON object with one nonempty prompt string of at most 8000 characters.","tier":1}
